rule.pooled_per_arm: accepted tasks per hour over the summed clock (implementer-accepted for G and T, accepted for S), makespan as the mean run, GPU-hours per accepted task (chat-server ms / accepted), worker-hours per accepted task for T, per-task acceptance table
rule.build: ratio >= 1.5 AND T has the shortest makespan AND T's accepted-per-run >= best arm - 1
rule.no_s_alone: S has the shortest makespan at acceptance >= T's -> no: run the GPU implementer alone; the review loop stays only as an optional quality gate (checked before the marginal band)
rule.marginal: ratio in [1.2, 1.5) OR T's makespan within 10% of the shortest -> the user decides, with GPU-hours per accepted in front of them
rule.reviewer_health: per arm (G, T): reviews still without a verdict after the verdict turn > 2 -> inconclusive, fix the reviewer, rerun all arms; capped first reviews and timeouts are reported per arm, not decisive (ruling: the spec's 'capped after the verdict turn' read as 'still without a verdict'; every capped review would make the window inconclusive at W3's rate)
rule.bootstrap: paired per-task bootstrap CI (n_boot 10000, seed 20261010) of T's bottleneck seconds per accepted task (task wall / 3) minus the better of S/G's (task wall), over tasks accepted in every run of both arms: REPORTED, not decisive
rule.user_lane: probe p50 reported per run (wf-user-probe.py, 60 s); not a decision clause in round 2 (user: chat usability during runs does not matter)
rule.code: analysis.round2_decide via `cli.py w3 --round2`; bar 1.5, marginal 1.2, R2_NONE_LIMIT 2

void: tasks the transcript scan finds tainted, applied to every run of all arms (cli.py w3 --round2 --void)
probe: wf-user-probe.py in LXC 153, owner key, 60 s interval; 30-sample idle baseline per window
prior_observations_disclosed: W3 (old reviewer): one T run vs a partial G baseline gave 1.39x throughput (marginal under the old 2x rule), equal quality, user lane 1.74x; 7 of 27 reviews capped with no verdict
